# eShop Reference Application - "AdventureWorks"

A reference .NET application implementing an e-commerce website using a services-based architecture using [.NET Aspire](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire/).

![eShop Reference Application architecture diagram](img/eshop_architecture.png)

![eShop homepage screenshot](img/eshop_homepage.png)

## Getting Started

This version of eShop is based on .NET 9. 

Previous eShop versions:
* [.NET 8](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/tree/release/8.0)

### Prerequisites

- Clone the eShop repository: https://github.com/dotnet/eshop
- [Install & start Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/)

#### Windows with Visual Studio
- Install [Visual Studio 2022 version 17.10 or newer](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/).
  - Select the following workloads:
    - `ASP.NET and web development` workload.
    - `.NET Aspire SDK` component in `Individual components`.
    - Optional: `.NET Multi-platform App UI development` to run client apps

Or

- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configure your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required and included in the script below.)

```powershell
install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense -Force
$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vside.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
```

Or

- From Dev Home go to `Machine Configuration -> Clone repositories`. Enter the URL for this repository. In the confirmation screen look for the section `Configuration File Detected` and click `Run File`.

#### Mac, Linux, & Windows without Visual Studio
- Install the latest [.NET 9 SDK](https://dot.net/download?cid=eshop)

Or

- Run the following commands in a Powershell & Terminal running as `Administrator` to automatically configuration your environment with the required tools to build and run this application. (Note: A restart is required after running the script below.)

##### Install Visual Studio Code and related extensions
```powershell
install-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.Configuration -AllowPrerelease -AcceptLicense  -Force
$env:Path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
get-WinGetConfiguration -file .\.configurations\vscode.dsc.yaml | Invoke-WinGetConfiguration -AcceptConfigurationAgreements
```

> Note: These commands may require `sudo`

- Optional: Install [Visual Studio Code with C# Dev Kit](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/csharp/get-started)
- Optional: Install [.NET MAUI Workload](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/maui/get-started/installation?tabs=visual-studio-code)

## What this is

**eShop ("AdventureWorks") — a .NET 10 / .NET Aspire reference e‑commerce application built as a set of microservices** wired together by an Aspire AppHost, communicating over HTTP/gRPC and a RabbitMQ integration‑event bus, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis (`README.md:1`, `eShop.slnx:1`).

## The composition root

`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs` is the single runnable entry point of the solution (`Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, `OutputType=Exe`, `src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj:1`). It builds a `DistributedApplication` and runs it (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:3`, `:103`). It composes:

**Infrastructure containers** — Redis `redis` (`:7`), RabbitMQ `eventbus` (`:8`), PostgreSQL `postgres` on the `ankane/pgvector` image (`:10`) with four databases: `catalogdb`, `identitydb`, `orderingdb`, `webhooksdb` (`:15-18`).

**Processes started (9 .NET projects + 1 proxy)**

| Aspire resource | Project | Kind of process |
|---|---|---|
| `identity-api` (`:23`) | Identity.API | ASP.NET MVC + Duende IdentityServer; `AddIdentityServer` / `UseIdentityServer` / `MapDefaultControllerRoute` (`src/Identity.API/Program.cs:18`, `:51`, `:55`). External HTTP, health `/health` (`:24-26`) |
| `basket-api` (`:30`) | Basket.API | **gRPC-only** service: `MapGrpcService<BasketService>()` (`src/Basket.API/Program.cs:12`) exposing `GetBasket`/`UpdateBasket`/`DeleteBasket` (`src/Basket.API/Proto/basket.proto:7-10`); uses Redis + RabbitMQ (`:31-32`) |
| `catalog-api` (`:36`) | Catalog.API | Minimal-API HTTP service, versioned group `api/catalog` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:16`), items/brands/types CRUD and semantic-relevance search (`:21-107`) |
| `ordering-api` (`:40`) | Ordering.API | Minimal-API `api/orders` (`src/Ordering.API/Apis/OrdersApi.cs:9-17`), authorization required (`src/Ordering.API/Program.cs:21`) |
| `order-processor` (`:46`) | OrderProcessor | Worker SDK project (`src/OrderProcessor/OrderProcessor.csproj:1`) hosting `GracePeriodManagerService : BackgroundService` (`src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:18`, `src/OrderProcessor/Services/GracePeriodManagerService.cs:8`). Waits for ordering-api because that project owns the EF migrations (`:49`) |
| `payment-processor` (`:51`) | PaymentProcessor | Headless event consumer: subscribes to `OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent` (`src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:5-6`) |
| `webhooks-api` (`:54`) | Webhooks.API | Minimal-API `/api/webhooks` (`src/Webhooks.API/Apis/WebHooksApi.cs:11`) plus event subscriptions (`src/Webhooks.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:21-23`) |
| `mobile-bff` (`:60`) | YARP reverse proxy (no project) | `builder.AddYarp("mobile-bff").ConfigureMobileBffRoutes(...)` fronting catalog/ordering/identity (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:185-224`) |
| `webhooksclient` (`:65`) | WebhookClient | Blazor Server app; also `MapAuthenticationEndpoints()` and `MapPost("/webhook-received")` (`src/WebhookClient/Program.cs:26-30`, `src/WebhookClient/Endpoints/WebhookEndpoints.cs:31`) |
| `webapp` (`:69`) | WebApp | The storefront: Blazor interactive-server Razor components (`src/WebApp/Program.cs:31`) plus an image forwarder `/product-images/{id}` → catalog-api (`:33`). External HTTP, references basket/catalog/ordering + RabbitMQ (`:70-77`) |

Every service also gets `MapDefaultEndpoints()`, which maps `/health` and `/alive` in development (`src/eShop.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs:108-121`).

## Non-HTTP entry points (message consumers)

RabbitMQ subscriptions are a second class of entry point: Basket (`OrderStartedIntegrationEvent`, `src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:19`), Catalog (2 handlers, `src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:32-33`), Ordering.API (5 handlers, `src/Ordering.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:55-59`), Webhooks.API (3, `src/Webhooks.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:21-23`), WebApp (6, `src/WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs:45-50`), PaymentProcessor (1, `src/PaymentProcessor/Program.cs:6`).

## Runnable but *not* started by the AppHost

`ClientApp` (.NET MAUI, multi-target android/ios/maccatalyst/windows, `src/ClientApp/ClientApp.csproj:4`, `:16`) and `HybridApp` (MAUI Blazor Hybrid, `src/HybridApp/HybridApp.csproj:4`, `:16`) are `Exe` client apps in the solution but are never referenced in `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs` — they must be launched separately. The remaining projects (`EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, `WebAppComponents`, `eShop.ServiceDefaults`) are libraries, not processes.

Two optional compositions are present but disabled by hardcoded flags: OpenAI/Azure OpenAI and Ollama enrichment of catalog-api/webapp (`src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:80-90`) — with `useOpenAI`/`useOllama` set to `false`, so no Ollama container starts by default.

One caveat: I read this from source rather than by running it — the repo-analysis tool failed on this solution, so the process list above is derived from the AppHost graph and project SDK types, not from an observed run.
